item.title: Reduce JNI copies and optimize guarded Unicorn2 memory paths
item.description:
Summary

This PR reduces Java/JNI copies and temporary allocations, improves ELF lookup/loading paths, and adds bounded Unicorn2 optimizations for RAM backing reuse, guest-store mapping lookup and repeated ARM exits.

The changes use guarded fallbacks. They do not introduce application-specific dispatch, replace guest algorithms, change the default backend or advertise different CPU features. Native patches and build notes accompany the updated Linux x86_64 library; other platforms have not been rebuilt or newly validated here.

Performance evidence and limits

Historical testing compared upstream 2ba8156 with checkpoint cae8988: across eight equally weighted workloads, work-time speedup was 1.460x, process-wall speedup 1.438x, and peak-RSS ratio 0.825. These are results for that historical checkpoint, not a fresh benchmark of this synchronized PR.

The later guarded-wide-store increment was measured separately against cae8988, with about 5.3% lower aggregate long-work time. Do not multiply the separate results. Some cold stages regressed, small-map/TT cold RSS increased about 1.5% in the historical comparison, and later confirmation observed roughly 5 ms higher JNA startup time. The included reports retain these adverse results and uncertainties. No universal speedup or non-increasing-memory guarantee is claimed.

Validation

The branch starts from upstream 2ede14d and has identical production blobs to the tested synchronization merge in the fork.

  • All modules completed test compilation on Linux x86_64 / JDK 8, with test compilation explicitly enabled.
  • 62 tests in 27 passing classes retained in this PR passed through isolated JUnitCore runs. Four additional fork-local regression checks also passed but their test sources are not included here.
  • All 11 newly added upstream test classes (19 tests) passed.
  • Eight representative workload smokes passed, checking the actually loaded native SHA256.
  • ARM32/ARM64 JNI table review preserved all 229 slot-to-handler bindings. The accepted native artifact was unchanged during upstream synchronization.

This is not a claim that the full Maven/CI suite is green. Surefire was missing locally and Maven Central DNS was unavailable. Hypervisor/KVM, legacy Unicorn and several iOS sample failures were reproduced on the pre-merge checkpoint; the iOS ClassDump64 native abort remains unresolved and is not counted as a pass. See docs/performance/UPSTREAM_PR_VALIDATION.md in this branch for details.

Review scope

This is a single clean commit containing production changes, native patches/build notes and concise evidence. It does not add benchmark/sample code, timing scripts, raw logs or held experimental implementations. Existing upstream tests remain unchanged.

Ready for review of the combined Java/JNI and Unicorn2 scope.

item.title: ApkFile.getPackageName: tolerate a malformed/minimal resources.arsc
item.description:
Problem. createDalvikVM() → BaseVM.findLibrary() → ApkFile.getPackageName() calls apk-parser's getApkMeta(), whose full parse reads the resource table. An APK whose resources.arsc is the minimal stub aapt2 emits for a resource-less app makes that parse throw:

java.nio.BufferUnderflowException
  at net.dongliu.apk.parser.parser.ResourceTableParser.readChunkHeader
  ...
  at com.github.unidbg.linux.android.dvm.apk.ApkFile.getPackageName(ApkFile.java:97)
  at com.github.unidbg.linux.android.dvm.BaseVM.findLibrary(BaseVM.java:276)

BufferUnderflowException is a RuntimeException, so neither the ParserException nor the IOException catch handles it, and loading the APK fails outright.

Fix. The package name is a literal attribute on the <manifest> element and needs no resource table. Catch the RuntimeException and read it straight from the binary AndroidManifest.xml (via the existing getFileData, a plain zip read); rethrow only if even that yields nothing. Normal APKs are unaffected — the fallback runs only on the exception path. One file, no API change.

Validation. The added binary-manifest reader was unit-tested standalone against stub-arsc APKs and recovers the real package name (e.g. re.lab.app01); ApkFile.java compiles against apk-parser 2.6.10. I couldn't run unidbg's full test suite locally — happy to adjust.

Found while using unidbg to emulate a .so in an APK that had no resources.

item.title: 增加支持在LinuxModule注册新的符号
item.description:
背景: 在模拟一个elf的文件执行时,该elf需要用到libdl.so的dlvsym函数,但我看了下unidbg带的so中仅支持dlsym函数，于是我手动实现该函数，并通过registerSvc注册进SvcMemory,再通过registerSymbol函数注册到libdl的Module里。

问题:当我注册进去后发现, elf中依旧找不到dlvsym函数，而我尝试通过module.findSymbolByName()和memory.dlsym()去寻找，依旧找不到dlvsym函数。

发现:我看了一下代码，对于系统库的LinuxMoudle而言,发现findSymbolByName仅从缓存和elf文件结构中寻找符号，而registerSymbol函数仅将符号添加到hook表，也就是说registerSymbol实际上只支持对elf文件中的符号进行hook(替换)，而无法添加符号函数。

解决:我认为如果仅是对现有符号进行hook，这非真正意义上的注册符号，所以我认为registerSymbol除了hook，应该还支持进行增加符号。

item.title: 修复在threadDispatcher启用时，socket相关的读取造成的死锁问题
item.description:
在threadDispatcherEnabled时，由于使用抢先式调度，会导致socketpair在其中一个线程在接收时，持续占用调度，导致永远无法接收到发送线程的信息。

同理，由于ppoll没有考虑io是否有信息可读，会导致线程持续卡死在后接的recv中，导致实际运行逻辑与实际不符，同时如果其他线程正在同一socket准备发送请求，也会造成死锁。

详细样例可见本fork的master分支
